capability: crew dispatch: a Commander parent blocking on run_crew.py while a child crew runs
constraint: decision:no-reaping -- nothing marks an entry/lease abandoned, expires it, or force-claims anything
decision:fail-toward-alive -- ambiguity resolves toward alive, never toward dead
decision: decision:registry-before-staleness -- tried first: staleness is judged entirely inside fenced checklist_engine.py (_is_stale/require_session), which no owned file reads today, so the registry-consultation direction has no seam in owned files without touching the fence. @grade: guess · leans g1-implement · settle: tried; floating the parent-self-heartbeat alternative per the pre-ruling's own settle clause instead of escalating, since it needs zero checklist_engine.py changes -- this is also fix direction 1 named explicitly in the original GitHub issue #607 ('heartbeat from the launcher rather than from the engine's mutating verbs'), not an invented mechanism

implementation choice (this run, in-latitude, not floated): a context-managed background thread reads the DISPATCHING process's own ambient os.environ SPINE_FILE/SPINE_SESSION (never the child's derived env), no-ops when either is unset, and every PARENT_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SECONDS=300 (well under the engine's 1800s lease_stale_seconds) calls checklist_engine.load() -> checklist_engine.heartbeat(cl, session_id) -> checklist_engine.save() directly (run_crew.py already `import checklist_engine`, no subprocess/CLI round-trip needed). stop_event.set() + thread.join() happens in a finally around the blocking call, BEFORE control returns to any caller that might issue its own mutating verb against the same spine -- this ordering is load-bearing (prevents the heartbeat thread racing the next mutating call).

NO self-collision guard (cold-critic finding #2, fixed before dispatch): a first draft skipped heartbeating when the child's env carried the same SPINE_FILE/SPINE_SESSION as the parent's own -- but crew_env()'s documented contract means that IS the common case (a handoff-only dispatch with no --spine inherits the dispatcher's ambient SPINE_FILE/SPINE_SESSION unchanged), so that guard would have disabled the fix for most ordinary crew dispatches, exactly where it matters most. checklist_engine.heartbeat() already refuses a session_id that does not own the lease (:1174), so a child sharing the parent's identity is BY CONSTRUCTION the same owner, not a collision -- heartbeating is correct there, not dangerous. The only residual risk is an ordinary last-writer-wins race on the single last_heartbeat field if the child also happens to mutate that spine concurrently -- bounded (self-heals next 300s tick), and strictly preferable to leaving a live parent reading stale (decision:fail-toward-alive). Run unconditionally whenever the DISPATCHING process's own ambient vars are set.
evidence: a real checklist_engine.py-backed spine with a lease claimed and its last_heartbeat artificially aged past 1800s, then a real blocking run_crew.py dispatch (interval monkeypatched small) driven in a fresh process, asserting `current`/claim no longer reads stale -- not reasoned about from inside the dispatching session
no-ambient-vars case: most dispatches have no SPINE_FILE/SPINE_SESSION at all -- assert no thread starts and no behavior changes (honest-null path)

shared-spine case (cold-critic finding #2): a dispatch with no explicit --spine, so the child's env inherits the SAME SPINE_FILE/SPINE_SESSION as the parent -- assert the heartbeat thread still starts and still advances last_heartbeat (the fix must not silently disable itself in the common case)

triage_candidates.statement: checklist_engine.save() appears to be a non-atomic read-modify-write with no file locking. g1's parent-lease-heartbeat fix introduces a new concurrent writer onto a spine file the dispatched child crew may also write to during the same block (the common shared-spine case). At the 300s production interval the collision window is narrow, but it is a new concurrency pattern this fix introduces. Recommend confirming save()'s write is safe under this pattern (atomic rename, or a documented last-write-wins argument for heartbeat-only fields) as a follow-up -- checklist_engine.py is fenced from this run's own scope.
